source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use the calculated equianalgesic dose without reduction because published conversion factors account completely for cross-tolerance and individual response.","B":"Increase the calculated dose of the new opioid because incomplete cross-tolerance makes the replacement opioid predictably less potent.","C":"Use the equianalgesic calculation as an estimate and generally begin the new opioid below the calculated dose when appropriate because cross-tolerance and patient response vary.","D":"Match the number and strength of tablets between opioids because equianalgesic estimates are unnecessary when both medications are given orally."}}
source_row.rationale: CDC cautions that opioid conversion factors are estimates and should not be used as exact dosing equivalents for switching. A lower starting dose of the new opioid is generally used to account for incomplete cross-tolerance and variability.
